proves: NOTHING IS CORRECT IN ROW 0. This image pins a known defect.
defect: row 0 sets align-items:baseline; the three runs align on their BOX BOTTOMS, not their baselines
checkable: 360x190, two rows of three runs at 14, 22 and 34 point, each run's first glyph an H whose ink bottom is its baseline. The three runs occupy x=16..41, 51..89 and 100..158 in both rows. Row 0, align-items:baseline, spans y=29..64: the H bottoms are 61, 58 and 56 - five pixels apart where all three should share one y. Row 1, align-items:flex-start and the control, spans y=98..139: H bottoms 108, 117 and 132, which is what flex-start means and must not move. Read the H rather than the run: the runs carry descenders, so a run's lowest ink is below its baseline by an amount that grows with the font size, and comparing those would report three numbers that differ for a second reason.
cause: taffy discards a measured leaf's baseline and then reads the missing value as the leaf's full height. compute_leaf_layout returns first_baselines: Point::NONE unconditionally at taffy-0.13.0/src/compute/leaf.rs:102 and :157, and flexbox falls back to the height at flexbox.rs:1522, :1524, :2037 and :2047. A leaf's baseline is therefore its bottom edge.
not-ours: this renderer measures the baseline and keeps it: layout.rs:173 stores first_baseline in LayoutResult::baselines, and the comment there says why it has to be captured in the measure closure - taffy takes the size and drops the rest. There is no path through TaffyTree by which a measured leaf can report one, because the measure closure returns Size<f32>.
v1-too: not a v2 regression. v1 exposes BASELINE as an align value (canvas.type.ts:447) and calls setMeasureFunc (text.canvas.ts:72) but never setBaselineFunc, and Yoga's default baseline for a childless measured leaf is its height - taffy's fallback exactly. v1 aligns box bottoms for the same reason.
grid-too: grid routes leaves through the same compute_leaf_layout, and taffy additionally carries `TODO: Support baseline alignment in the vertical axis` at grid/mod.rs:342 and :528. Extending this fixture to a grid would pin the same defect twice rather than find a different answer.
chrome: measured in Chrome on the equivalent CSS, ink threshold 128, reading the FULL WORD's ink including descenders. Row 0 (align-items: baseline): tops 46, 39, 29 and bottoms 59, 60, 62 for 14px, 22px, 34px. Row 1 (align-items: flex-start, the control): tops 99, 101, 106 and bottoms 112, 122, 139.
the_defect_has_a_sign: ours run 62, 60, 56 - decreasing. The trend is inverted, which is what a shared bottom edge does: align the boxes and the largest text sits highest. This matters more than the spread: a fix that narrowed the gap while keeping the order wrong would pass a 'how far apart' test and fail this one. Correct is 59, 60, 62 or the same trend at whatever offset the port leaves.
measured: H has no descender, so its ink bottom IS the baseline. Row 0 H-bottoms are 5px apart; row 1 (align-items:flex-start, the control) is expected to differ and does.
correct-looks-like: all three H-bottoms in row 0 share one y. Row 1 is unaffected and must not change.
upstream: known and already fixed. taffy issue #199; PR #1091 merged to main on 2026-08-10, two days after 0.13.0 shipped and therefore not in any release we can depend on. Nothing was filed by us and there was nothing to file. This is a version bump rather than a code change: raise taffy past 0.13 and re-accept this image. Until then the workaround, if one were ever wanted, is a tree implementing LayoutPartialTree itself, since LayoutOutput::from_sizes_and_baselines exists and only the TaffyTree measure path cannot reach it.
status: the control row is measured against Chrome and matches. Row 0 PINS A DEFECT - re-accept when baseline alignment is fixed, and check the *sign* rather than the spread. The numbers moved by 1, 2 and 0 rows when the text port landed, which is per-size strut rounding changing the box heights this defect aligns the bottoms of - a consequence, not a regression.
the-defect-has-a-sign-and-that-is-what-t: Chrome's row 0 bottoms INCREASE with size - 59, 60, 62 - because aligned baselines let a larger descender hang further below the line. Ours DECREASE - 65, 64, 63 - which is what aligning box bottoms does: a shared bottom edge puts the small text's ink lowest. The trend is inverted, not merely offset. A fix that closed the spread but kept the order wrong would pass a 'the baselines should be level' test and fail this one, which is why the target recorded here is Chrome's 59/60/62 rather than the spec sentence.
two-different-bottoms-live-in-this-scene: the word is Hxgp, so its full-word ink bottom is a descender and its leftmost glyph's bottom is the baseline. They are different numbers and only one is comparable with Chrome's: full-word 65, 64, 63 against Chrome's 59, 60, 62; leftmost-glyph 62, 60, 56, which is where the 'baselines six apart' reading comes from. Row 1 is what proves which quantity Chrome's numbers are - its tops 99, 101, 106 match ours exactly and its bottoms 112, 122, 139 match our full-word 112, 122, 140.
the-control-row-matches-chrome: row 1's tops are 99, 101, 106 in both, so the port places text where Chrome places it and the divergence is isolated to the row that asks for baseline alignment. The one-row difference at 34px, 140 against 139, is the faintest antialiased row landing either side of the threshold.
what-moved-when-text-left-the-paragraph: this image moved by 1, 2 and 0 rows for the 14px, 22px and 34px words when text moved off SkParagraph onto line boxes computed here. That is what rounding the strut PER SIZE looks like - Chrome rounds fontBoundingBoxAscent and descent to whole pixels and so do we now, and each size rounds by a different amount. The defect did not change; its arithmetic input did. A fixture pinning a defect moves whenever the defect's inputs move, which is not the same as a fixture pinning correct behaviour moving.
whose-defect: taffy's, and out of this renderer's reach: compute/leaf.rs returns first_baselines: Point::NONE for every measured leaf, unconditionally, in both of its return paths. Our measurer computes a first baseline and keeps it in LayoutResult for the painter, but nothing can hand it to the flex algorithm, so align-items: baseline falls back to aligning box bottoms. Issue #199, fixed in PR #1091 two days after the release pinned here.
